pages.title: Start with an existing corpus
pages.description: Adopt one complete canonical corpus in place, from the CLI or the desktop application.

blocks.content:
spis corpus adopt /absolute/path/to/unpacked-corpus
spis corpus status

blocks.text: The selected directory must contain canonical `example-catalogs.json`; each indexed catalog must carry matching `sources.json` and `references.json`; and every indexed `reference.json` file must retain the full-product-reference schema, evidence status, and evidence gaps. Spis validates that complete graph before atomically writing `~/.config/spis/corpus.json`.

The corpus stays in place. Subsequent corpus commands and Spis Desktop resolve the saved root, so original provenance, screenshots, recordings, receipts, and other referenced files are not copied into a reduced store. Re-adopting the same canonical path reports every reference unchanged and creates no duplicate.

On first launch, Choose Corpus opens a native directory picker and sends only the selected path to Spis's loopback API. The API invokes the same `corpus adopt` operation as the CLI; Swift does not parse or copy a corpus. The same control remains under Manage, beside Show it again for replaying onboarding.

items: ZIP, tar, gzip, bzip2, xz, zstd, 7z, and rar archives are refused with an instruction to unpack them first.

A missing or noncanonical index, duplicate or unsafe catalog slug, escaping path or symlink, mismatched schema or catalog identity, missing record file, count mismatch, or record without evidence status and evidence gaps refuses the whole adoption. The previous saved corpus remains active.

CLI JSON reports state, root, catalog, reference and file counts, index SHA-256, imported, unchanged, conflicting, rejected, and a result message. Desktop keeps that exact output or refusal selectable.

pages.title: Brama decisions
pages.description: The settings Spis reads to ask Brama, and what an unset one does.

items: `MODEL_ROUTER_URL` — the Brama address. Unset or blank: the command that asks Brama is refused, naming the variable and what it holds.
`MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL` — a Brama model alias. Unset or blank: the command that asks Brama is refused, naming the variable and what it holds.

`MODEL_ROUTER_TOKEN_ROLE` — the vault role reference ROLE#FIELD whose value Stado, or SPIS_CREDENTIALS_FILE, gives and Spis sends as the bearer. Unset or blank: the question is sent with no bearer; a value that is not ROLE#FIELD, or a secret that cannot be read, is refused.

`SPIS_CREDENTIALS_FILE` — an owner-only JSON file of role -> field -> value that answers MODEL_ROUTER_TOKEN_ROLE in Stado's place. Unset or blank: the reference is read with `stado credentials get --role` (STADO_BIN names another Stado program); a file other users can read, or one without the role or field, is refused.

`SPIS_DECISION_CHAT_MODEL` — a model of the OpenAI-compatible service at MODEL_ROUTER_URL, asked through /v1/chat/completions instead of Brama's decision route. Unset or blank: typed questions go to Brama's POST /v1/decisions under MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL.

blocks.text: Every question Spis asks Brama is one typed decision on `POST /v1/decisions`: a `choice` among the options the question declares, so the answer is one of them or the command is refused with what Brama sent. A refusal is kept with Brama's status and body; an unreachable Brama is named with its address.
`MODEL_ROUTER_MODEL` takes `decision-model` or `best-decision-model`; `best` asks `best-decision-model`. Any other alias is refused before a question is sent, naming the aliases the route answers.

blocks.text: Each catalog is one family of reference examples, kept as attributed records with their evidence and their evidence gaps. A catalog whose records are of several kinds counts each kind: the presentation catalog, for one, separates strategy-consulting decks, academic research talks, thesis defences, startup pitches, investor presentations, policy briefings and the rest, so a deck can be compared with references of its own kind.
